Its Gram kernel is explicit: current-current entries are min(i,j), current-future entries are i*b_K(n), and the future-future block is K*b_K(n)b_K(m). The complete diagonal is at most (14K^2+1)/12<=(5/4)K^2 and is summable after the RH weight. Applying Green-Tao's finite Vaughan identity componentwise on (K,2K] and (2K,4K] before taking the norm gives B_K=-V_(I,K)+V_(II,K), so the RH-equivalent target is exactly sum_K K^(-2-alpha)||-V_(I,K)+V_(II,K)||_2^2<infinity.
claims.proof_boundary: The bounded feature representation, explicit Gram blocks, arbitrary-vector expansion, diagonal envelope, signed off-diagonal criterion, two finite interval reconstructions, and componentwise vector Vaughan identity are exact or source-backed and independently checked. Vaughan is applied before squaring, so the decisive Type I/II cancellation remains inside the vector norm. Coefficientwise control gives only H_K=O(K^3), one full power above the summable scale; a uniform coordinate estimate o(K) still gives only o(K^3). The all-interval H*log^(-A)X theorem for H>=X^(5/8+epsilon), applied coordinatewise, remains at K^3*log^(-2A)K and does not supply the correlated vector square estimate. Separate Type I and Type II norm bounds are not equivalent to their signed difference. No vector Type I/II power gain, full Burnol bound, RH, PF-infinity, or Lambda <= 0 is proved.

claims.title: Mixed-boundary sine and modewise Vaughan handoff
claims.claim: The min(i,j) Gram underlying the ordinary anchored suffix vector has an exact mixed Dirichlet-Neumann sine spectrum: theta_(K,r)=(2r-1)pi/(2K+1), phi_(K,r)(i)=2sin(i theta_(K,r))/sqrt(2K+1), and lambda_(K,r)=[4sin^2(theta_(K,r)/2)]^(-1). Unfolding the terminal anchor makes every spectral coefficient X_(K,r) one compact ordinary-Mobius test with coefficients at most 2/sqrt(2K+1). The reciprocal-tail criterion is uniformly equivalent to the half-odd square function sum_K K^(-alpha)sum_r |X_(K,r)|^2/(2r-1)^2. Applying finite Vaughan mode by mode before squaring gives X_(K,r)=-T_(I,K,r)+T_(II,K,r), yielding an exact additive-twist Type I/II square-function target.
claims.proof_boundary: The mixed-boundary inverse Laplacian, sine orthogonality, eigenpairs, arbitrary-vector reconstruction, anchor unfolding, feature envelope, eigenvalue comparison, odd-frequency equivalence, and both finite Vaughan interval identities are exact or source-backed and independently checked. Absolute feature bounds, generic Parseval, Davenport's arbitrary-logarithmic estimate, and scalar all-interval logarithmic cancellation all leave the normalized K^(1-alpha) scale, one full power short. Uniform square-root-plus-epsilon cancellation in the unnormalized half-odd sine brackets would suffice when 2epsilon<alpha, but is conditional only. Separate absolute Type I and Type II mode bounds are not equivalent to their signed difference. No additive-twist square-root theorem, signed modewise Type I/II gain, full Burnol bound, RH, PF-infinity, or Lambda <= 0 is proved.

claims.title: Spectral anchor and summable high-mode reduction
claims.claim: The half-odd spectral coefficient splits exactly as X_(K,r)=Y_(K,r)+beta_K h_(K,r), where the current-block modes satisfy sum_r|Y_(K,r)|^2<=K and the endpoint amplitude satisfies |h_(K,r)|^2<=2/K. For every 1<=R<=K this gives the high-mode bound sum_(r>R)|X_(K,r)|^2/(2r-1)^2<=2K/(2R+1)^2+4|beta_K|^2/[K(2R+1)]. Using |beta_K|<=2K and R_(alpha,K)=ceil(K^(1-alpha/2)), the normalized high tail is at most 2K^(-1)+8K^(-alpha/2), hence dyadically summable. The RH-equivalent reciprocal-tail criterion is therefore exactly equivalent, for each fixed 0<alpha<1, to the spectral square restricted to r<=R_(alpha,K).
claims.proof_boundary: The current/anchor split, endpoint phase, endpoint envelope, current-block Parseval identity, odd-frequency tail estimate, current and anchor high-mode inequalities, unconditional cutoff, dyadic summability, and reduced low-mode equivalence are exact and independently checked. The cutoff is pointwise in each fixed alpha>0 and supplies neither alpha=0 nor uniformity as alpha tends to zero. Pullback to the ordinary-Mobius support gives an entrywise-positive kernel G whose per-scale diagonal is uniformly less than 7pi^2/24. The fixed theta split gives exact component formulas for J_(n,t) and J_(n,t)' and rational B_0/B_1 bars: either strict first-block inequality excludes a common zero at that point. The bars grow polynomially and are explicitly limited to compact-frequency use. A positive Newman boundary is exactly a common nonzero real zero of J_t and J_t'. At t=0 this is tangential contact of A_0 with the unit-exponential characteristic function 1/(1+x^2).
